license: Public domain. Commons tags {{PD-France}} {{PD-1996}} {{PD-US-expired}} (published 1925, so expired in the US). Original: BnF Estampes et photographie, EI-13 (1236), Gallica btv1b53150713f.
credit_line: Agence Rol, 1925 / Bibliothèque nationale de France (public domain)
what_it_shows: HERO. The Eiffel Tower at night in 1925, covered in the Citroën illuminations (lit up from July 1925), seen across the Seine. Same year as the scam. Plate numbers 'ROL 102414' are written across the top edge.
best_segments: S1 hook ('sold the Eiffel Tower for scrap'). Slow push-in on the tower. Crop the top 5% to remove the plate numbers. Portrait-native, so it fills 9:16.

license: Public domain. Commons tags {{PD-France}} {{PD-1996}} {{PD-US-expired}}. BnF EI-13 (2771), Meurisse 24449 A.
credit_line: Agence Meurisse, 1925 / Bibliothèque nationale de France (public domain)
what_it_shows: A wide night shot of the Seine with the Arts Décoratifs exhibition lights and the illuminated tower far off. Landscape. The tower is small in frame.
best_segments: Establishing or transition shot ('Paris, 1925' on-screen text). Pan from right to left along the river. Weak for 9:16 unless you pan.

license: Public domain dedication. Commons tag {{CC-zero}} (Rijksmuseum RP-F-2012-96-168, handle http://hdl.handle.net/10934/RM0001.COLLECT.557655). Underlying postcard is from 1925, so it is also PD in the US by age.
what_it_shows: A blue-tinted 1925 postcard: 'Exposition des Arts Décoratifs, La Tour Eiffel vue de nuit', with the tower in a lattice of lights. The only colour-toned tower image. Faint mirrored 'Made in France' text shows through mid-frame.
best_segments: Alternate hook or end card. Portrait-native. The postcard title text could become an on-screen 'PARIS 1925' tag.

license: Public domain. Commons tags {{PD-France}} {{PD-1996}} {{PD-US-expired}}. BnF EI-13 (816), dated 1921.
credit_line: Agence Rol, 1921 / Bibliothèque nationale de France (public domain)
what_it_shows: The tower in daylight, shot from the Trocadéro over the gardens and the Pont d'Iéna. Tall and clean, with a Ferris-wheel-like structure on the right.
best_segments: S2 ('posing as a French official'): slow tilt up the tower. Also works as a daytime 'scrap value' beat with a '7,000 TONS (reported)' overlay.

license: Public domain. Commons tags {{PD-France}} {{PD-1996}} {{PD-US-expired}}. BnF EI-13 (635), dated 1919.
credit_line: Agence Rol, 1919 / Bibliothèque nationale de France (public domain)
what_it_shows: A misty, low-contrast view from the Champ de Mars, with pedestrians under the arch. Moody. Plate numbers run along the left edge.
best_segments: Backup tower shot. Its haze suits a 'too embarrassed to report it' beat. Crop the left 4%.

license: Public domain. Commons tags {{PD-Bain}} {{PD-old-70-1923}} {{LOC-image|id=ggbain.28362}}. Library of Congress, Bain News Service (no known restrictions).
credit_line: Bain News Service / Library of Congress (public domain)
what_it_shows: The façade of the Hôtel de Crillon on the Place de la Concorde, with captured WWI field guns parked in front. The guns point to c.1918-19, though Commons gives 1915. The caption 'HOTEL CRILLON, PARIS' is handwritten on the plate.
best_segments: S2 'secret meeting at a fancy hotel' (the hotel is from the legend). Crop to the façade above the guns, or keep the handwritten title for an archival feel. Landscape, so pan.

license: Public domain. Commons tags {{PD-USGov}} {{PD-old-70}}. The document is a US federal work: FBI Identification Order No. 1301, 10 Sep 1935, issued by J. Edgar Hoover. CAUTION: Commons got the scan from a Find a Grave user upload (findagrave.com memorial 176656691). The document is PD, but the scan's provenance is weak. It is low-res (1072px wide) with white margins.
credit_line: FBI / U.S. Department of Justice, Identification Order No. 1301 (1935), public domain
what_it_shows: BEST LUSTIG DOCUMENT. FBI 'WANTED' circular: 'ROBERT V. MILLER, true name VICTOR LUSTIG' with about 45 aliases ('COUNT LUSTIG', 'THE COUNT', 'THE SCARRED'), ten fingerprints, profile and front mugshots ('Photograph taken May 10, 1935'), a 'Viktor Lustig' signature, and the line 'wanted for escaping from the United States Detention Headquarters, New York City... September 1, 1935'. Lists a 'U.S. Secret Service, New York' arrest number.
best_segments: S4 (counterfeiting bust / result): push in from the WANTED header to the alias list to the mugshots. Hold on 'true name VICTOR LUSTIG'. The mugshot area is only about 250px tall, so don't go full-screen on the face.

license: Public domain. Commons tag {{PD-USGov-DOJ}}. US Department of Justice, Bureau of Investigation record dated 25 Jun 1931. Via the American Numismatic Society 'Funny Money' exhibit (web.archive.org/web/20150717162402/http://numismatics.org/Exhibits/FunnyMoney2d).
credit_line: U.S. Department of Justice, Bureau of Investigation (1931), public domain
what_it_shows: A 1931 BOI identification record: front and profile photos (high-contrast photocopy look), 'Charge: fugitive and con man', 'Residence: Coronado Hotel', 'Place of birth: Vienna Austria', 'international con man'. Typed criminal history mentions $29,000 in tampered Liberty Bonds and 'U.S. Secret Service Agent' James Haley.
best_segments: S2 hard cut to introduce 'Victor Lustig' (with a name super), or the S4 montage. Very low-res (460px): use it small, on a paper texture, or with heavy zoom only on the text.

license: Public domain (per Commons). Commons tag {{PD-US-not renewed}}. The photo is credited 'Picture by Evening Journal', from a 1935 Evening Public Ledger (Philadelphia) page. Non-renewal is asserted on Commons, not independently verified. Slightly riskier than the federal records.
credit_line: Evening Public Ledger (Philadelphia), 1935, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain, not renewed)
what_it_shows: Headline ''SMOOTHEST CON MAN EVER BORN!''. Lustig (centre) being questioned by U.S. agent Robert L. Godby and Secret Service agent Peter A. Rubano 'concerning the $52,000 counterfeit money found cached in a subway locker at Times Square.'
best_segments: S4 'counterfeiting bust': punch-in on the headline, then on Lustig's face. Best human-moment image of Lustig with the Secret Service. Low-res, so use a paper or newsprint treatment.

license: Public domain (underlying federal prison ID photo). Commons tag {{PD-USGov}}. CAUTION: this file is an iPhone 14 photo (EXIF date 2026-04-06) of a page in the French comic book 'L'homme qui vendit la Tour Eiffel'. The page carries the book's French caption and a '(PHOTO: COURTESY US NATIONAL ARCHIVES)' credit. Crop to the mugshot card only and drop the book caption. A clean scan from NARA San Francisco (Alcatraz 300-AZ case file) would be better.
credit_line: U.S. federal prison identification photo (National Archives), public domain
what_it_shows: A federal prison card 'No. 48065 Name Robert V. Miller', with profile and front mugshots of an older, bearded Lustig. Form code 'USPA—FLK—6-4-35'. NOT the Alcatraz number (300). 48065 is another federal institution's number and was not verified.
best_segments: S4 last beat ('landed him on Alcatraz'): front-face crop, slow zoom on the eyes. Highest-res face we have (front face about 700px tall in the original). Warm cast: grade to B&W.

license: Public domain per Commons tag {{PD-USGov-DOJ}}. CAUTION: the EXIF reads '© MaryRose Devine - Federal Reserve Bank of NY - 2010', so it is a 2010 photo of the note, not a DOJ work. A faithful flat reproduction of a PD 2-D object is not copyrightable in the US (Bridgeman v. Corel), so it is low risk, but the tag is wrong. Currency-image rules (31 CFR 411.1) allow motion-media use. Use B-roll only, never full-frame and photorealistic as a still.
credit_line: Counterfeit $10 note attributed to the Lustig–Watts ring, via American Numismatic Society / Wikimedia Commons
what_it_shows: A counterfeit 1928-series $10 Federal Reserve Note (Hamilton) attributed to Lustig's ring, engraved by William Watts, per the ANS caption.
best_segments: S4 'counterfeiting' word: quick 0.5 s flash or a slide-in under the VO. Low-res, so keep it small.

license: Public domain. Commons tag {{PD-USGov-Military-Navy}}. Official U.S. Navy photo NH 84546-KN, Naval History and Heritage Command.
credit_line: U.S. Navy / Naval History and Heritage Command (public domain)
what_it_shows: A hand-coloured 1930s view of Alcatraz Island (cellhouse, lighthouse, warden's house) with the battleship USS Oklahoma passing in front. Period-correct for Lustig's 1936 arrival.
best_segments: S4 'Alcatraz' payoff: crop the top band (island and cellhouse) to 9:16 and pan left to right. The ship takes up the lower half.
